title: Capacity Ledger and OKR Rhythm for Dedicated Scaling
creator: Priya Kaur
description: Create a quarter-long plan that maps Dedicated capacity commitments and elasticity policies to company OKRs via a single operational artifact we call the "capacity ledger". The ledger will codify commit windows, prewarm budgets, fallback lanes, and cost SLOs so PM/Eng/Ops can run predictable, measurable capacity rollouts across Q2. This ticket covers roadmap alignment, success metrics, high-level milestones, cross-team responsibilities, and a lightweight runbook for rollback and surge scenarios.
goals: Establish a capacity ledger that captures reserved pool commitments, allowable burst headroom, and prewarm schedules for each customer tier
Map ledger entries to quarterly OKRs and provide automated telemetry links so each OKR has measurable capacity/cost indicators
Reduce total dedicated pool token unit cost by 9-12% for target workloads through improved prewarm scheduling and smarter fallbacks
okrs: OKR-1: Improve Dedicated cost-effectiveness — reduce cost per 1M tokens by 10% (measured weekly via billing-telemetry dashboard)
OKR-2: Increase availability during surge windows — maintain P99 latency SLA below 350ms for top-10 customers while enabling 25% burst capacity
OKR-3: Operationalize rollouts — achieve <15 minute median recovery for capacity fallback tests across 3 simulated failure modes
milestones: 2026-03-10: Draft capacity ledger schema and sample entries (per-customer tier, region, prewarm cadence)
2026-03-25: Align ledger fields with Finance and Sales (committed months, billing reconciliation fields)
2026-04-08: Integrate ledger with Console telemetry — link ledger rows to SLO/time-series dashboards
2026-05-05: Run two canary rollouts using ledger policies (warm-pool shifts + fallback triggers)
2026-06-15: Final retro and OKR measurement report; lock settings for next quarter
acceptance_criteria: Capacity ledger defined and stored in accessible location (Confluence + Console metadata) with versioning
Automated dashboard panels show cost per-token and headroom utilization for ledger entries within 24 hours of ledger updates
Two canary rollouts completed with documented metrics and one playbook update resulting from findings
Finance and Sales sign-off on billing reconciliation fields and customer commitment mappings

risks: Ledger drift: teams may update pool settings outside ledger leading to mismatch between plan and runtime
Billing reconciliation complexity: mapping ledger commitments to invoicing lines requires Finance involvement and could delay rollouts
SLO regression: aggressive prewarm reductions could cause transient latency spikes for heavy tail customers
Cross-team bandwidth: Eng and Infra are already committed to other Q2 experiments and may constrain scope

Decision 2026-02-28: Start with three customer tiers (PLG-Free, Business, Enterprise) and two regions (us-west-2, eu-west-1) for MVP
Decision 2026-03-01: Canary cadence set to weekly windows in April; canary rollbacks automated via policy to fallback model variants
